operations: Main CSIR Scientia campus, Meiring Naude Road, Brummeria, Pretoria; ~3000 staff; multi-building research campus supplied by City of Tshwane on a time-of-use tariff with maximum-demand charge. Facilities Management & Security Services department runs energy efficiency/DSM; Strategic Procurement Unit tender@csir.co.za
scale_note: Pretoria campus electricity consumption 18.77 GWh/yr (CSIR RFP 3491, 2022). ~1.95 MWp on-site solar PV (558 kWp single-axis tracker 2015, 232 kWp dual-axis, 250 kWp rooftop 2017, 911 kWp rooftop 2019) covering roughly 15% of demand; >R14m saved since 2015. Energy Autonomous Campus programme target 8 MW PV / ~55% of demand plus 10 MW biogas baseload and wind; 2023 CSIR study found only more rooftop PV (to 50% of demand) financially viable. Municipal (Tshwane) supply >80%; no wheeling/PPA found.

operations: Curro Holdings: head office Durbanville (Cape Town); 81 campuses / 189 schools, 72 109 learners (Feb 2025), 818 000 m2 buildings on 595 ha, ~7 250 permanent staff; 41 campuses in Gauteng, 15 Western Cape. ADvTECH: head office 1 Waterstone Drive, Sandton; 122 schools (Crawford, Trinityhouse, Pinnacle, Abbotts etc.) and 34 tertiary campuses (Emeris/Varsity College, Vega, Rosebank College, IIE MSA) incl. new 47 000 m2 Emeris Sandton campus (Jan 2026). Both groups are many small dispersed municipal-supplied loads rather than one large site. ADvTECH ESG contact esg@advtech.co.za; Curro head of facilities not named publicly.
scale_note: Curro: not a large electricity consumer overall but daytime-concentrated load; Scope 2 17 712 tCO2e (2023, ~17-18 GWh equivalent); 21 solar PV installations and 38 battery systems by end-2023, further phased solar+battery roll-out (est. saving R200k/site/yr); R6m on back-up power H1 2025; facility costs (water, electricity, rates) +6.3% H1 2025; CDP score B; no wheeling/PPA found. ADvTECH: total energy 107 132 GJ in 2025 (~29.8 GWh) of which 6 428 GJ renewable (6%, own solar); Scope 2 28 080 tCO2e (2025); Scope 1+2 down 2.6% y/y; solar, boreholes and generators installed across campuses; no wheeling/PPA found.

operations: Seven campuses: South, North, Second Avenue, Bird Street, Missionvale (Gqeberha) and George; ~28 000 students; South Campus peak demand ~3 MW / base ~1.2 MW; supplied by Nelson Mandela Bay municipality on maximum-demand tariff. Infrastructure Services and Space Optimisation (ISSO) directorate under Senior Director Melvin Syce owns energy; Sustainability Services under Dr Andre Hefer runs the renewable programme.
scale_note: Electricity ~19.4 GWh (2020/21; 26.8 GWh 2018/19) and ~R60m/yr spend. 1 MW solar PV on South Campus since 2019 under a 10-yr PPA with Tasol Solar (university takes ownership after 10 yrs; ~16% of energy). 2022 Manco approved R65m more PV across all campuses; 4.4 MW / 8 500-panel solar platform now rolling out for ~25-30% of demand (saving R8-10m/yr). ALREADY CONTRACTED: 10-year renewable wheeling agreement with Etana Energy (licensed trader) for 50-55% of electricity from May 2027, procured via Nelson Mandela Bay Business Chamber electricity task team bid; CPI-linked pricing saving R2-2.5m/yr. Target ~80% renewable, ~12 000 tCO2/yr cut; R45m central generator model approved. Lat/lng from Wikipedia.

operations: NWU: three campuses (Potchefstroom, Mahikeng, Vanderbijlpark), ~950 buildings, ~300 municipal connections; peak demand PC 7.9 MW, MC 4.8 MW, VC 1.55 MW; Facilities dept with Engineering Compliance and Space & Utilities directorates. UKZN: five campuses in Durban and Pietermaritzburg (Westville HQ, Howard College, Medical School, Edgewood, PMB); Physical Planning and Facilities Management under ED Institutional Planning & Governance; procurement via Centralprocurement@ukzn.ac.za. UFS: Bloemfontein, South and Qwaqwa campuses, >500 000 m2 buildings, own 11 kV internal grid; University Estates under DVC People and Operations.
scale_note: NWU: grid electricity ~61.4 GWh (2023), 57.6 GWh total energy used 2024; R114m solar programme 2024-25 giving ~2.6 MWp Potchefstroom, 1.1 MWp Mahikeng, 385 kWp Vanderbijlpark (~4 MWp), est. saving ~R24m/yr; target min 30% renewable by 2025, reduce municipal connections 300 to 50 by 2028; aligned to USAf carbon-neutral-by-2050; HEFMA Renewable Energy award 2024; no wheeling/PPA found. UKZN: no published solar MW; Howard College hybrid microgrid study (2025) modelled R15.7m/yr savings; energy management via CMS; no wheeling/PPA found. UFS: 8 MW solar PV across three campuses (first plant 2017; Bloemfontein 3.7 MWp incl. two 1 MW ground-mounted plants plus Solar 4 and 5 adding 1.8 MW in 2025; Qwaqwa 918 kWp, South 759 kWp, Paradys 125 kWp), outright-purchase grid-tied without batteries; solar ~23% of needs (2023), >R94.3m saved to date; Qwaqwa diesel-solar microgrid; no wheeling/PPA found (Esterhuysen noted energy costs still rising with tariffs).

operations: SPU: city-centre university in Kimberley on North, Central and South campuses (Chapel St), ~9 031 students and 650 staff (Jan 2026), target 9 940 students by 2030; new-build campus with standby generators, TABS chilled-slab cooling and ring-main electrical reticulation; Facilities & Services, Infrastructure PMO and Property Management report to the COO, SCM to the CFO. SMU: single health-sciences campus at Ga-Rankuwa north of Pretoria next to Dr George Mukhari Academic Hospital, ~7 000 students; Built Environment directorate under Executive Director: Institutional Support. Lat/lng given is the SMU Ga-Rankuwa campus (Wikipedia); SPU is at Chapel St, Kimberley.
scale_note: SPU: no published solar MW or GWh; 2023 annual report tabulates available roof area for additional solar installations and a VRV heat-recovery project; strategic plan 2025-2029 proposes a Centre for Alternative Energy and campus energy-efficiency cost savings; notes lack of support from Sol Plaatje Municipality as an infrastructure threat. SMU: feasibility study (Spanish FIEM grant, MAI Group + Erinite Energy) for an on-site solar PV plant with storage launched Sept 2025 aiming at cost reduction, supply security and third-stream income; no MW, consumption or spend published; no wheeling/PPA found at either.

operations: Five campuses: Stellenbosch main campus, Tygerberg (medical), Bellville Park (business school), Worcester and Saldanha; ~32 000 students; supplied by Stellenbosch Municipality (which is itself procuring a 41.9 MW solar PV + 14.8 MWh BESS IPP under tender BSM 89/25, 2025). Facilities Management division (renamed Campus Development, Infrastructure and Services) under the COO runs energy, smart metering in all buildings, HVAC precinct plant and EPC programme; Net Zero Energy Plan being modelled with SU's Centre for Renewable and Sustainable Energy Studies (CRSES, 2025).
scale_note: Scope 1+2 footprint 84 453 tCO2e (ESP baseline) - implies roughly 70-80 GWh/yr electricity; ESP targets: carbon neutral by 2030, net zero by 2050 (some documents 2045), -10% municipal electricity by 2024 vs 2016, -20% Scope 2 by 2029 vs 2019; all new buildings Net Zero Carbon by 2030, all existing by 2050. Solar PV: 393 kWp Neelsie rooftop (R8m, Apr 2021), R74m Phase 1 rooftop programme of 4 667 kWp across Stellenbosch, Tygerberg, Bellville and Worcester (from 2022, 7.4-yr payback, 166 900 t CO2 over 25 yrs), 46.8 kWp STIAS net-zero building (2025); >R100m ESP project pipeline. No wheeling/PPA signed found; Net Zero Energy Plan explicitly assesses embedded generation and grid hosting capacity.

operations: Upper/Middle/Lower Main Campus in Rondebosch, Health Sciences campus (Observatory), Hiddingh, GSB Waterfront and residences; ~30 000 students; supplied by City of Cape Town at MV; Properties and Services (P&S) runs infrastructure, Environmental Sustainability Directorate in the VC's office runs energy/carbon strategy; EPCs done for all buildings >2 000 m2 (2022).
scale_note: Scope 2 electricity emissions 56 701 tCO2e in FY2024 (~60 GWh/yr equivalent, 64% on Main Campus); Scope 1+2 down 20% vs 2019. On-site PV small: ~95 MWh/yr from three sites (2024), ~300-400 kWp added late 2024 (Baxter, GSB, Meulenhof), Health Sciences central battery/solar/generator project awarded 2024; 2020 feasibility identified only ~2.5 MWp roof potential (heritage buildings). Net zero carbon/energy/water/waste by 2050 or sooner. ALREADY CONTRACTED: near-10-year PPA with licensed trader Discovery Green (signed 2 June 2026, after April 2025 Ampli Energy pilot and late-2024 tender) to wheel renewable energy equal to 70-90% of Main and Health Sciences campus consumption from Q3 2027 via City of Cape Town wheeling; ~33 200 tCO2e/yr cut; first trader PPA with a public university.

operations: TUT: ~60 000 students across nine+ campuses - Pretoria (Staatsartillerie Rd), Arcadia, Arts, Soshanguve North/South, Ga-Rankuwa, eMalahleni, Polokwane, Mbombela and new Giyani campus; Facilities/infrastructure under DVC: Operations; tenders via PURCO SA. CPUT: ~35-40 000 students, >180 buildings on Bellville (main), District Six/Cape Town, Granger Bay, Mowbray and Wellington campuses; Infrastructure Development and Facilities Management division under DVC: Operations; procurement www.cput.ac.za/services/procurement; hosts the South African Renewable Energy Technology Centre (SARETEC) and Green Hydrogen Centre of Specialisation at Bellville.
scale_note: TUT: no consolidated solar MW or GWh published; solar PV + storage tender for Building 10 Soshanguve South (TR 38-2024, 2025); eMalahleni campus alone uses ~650 MWh/yr (~R1.7m at R2.55/kWh) with a 150 kW PV proposal; Tshwane metro-funded solar streetlights at Pretoria West campus (2026). CPUT: no published solar MW or electricity spend; R565m infrastructure grant under scrutiny (2026 protests); no wheeling/PPA found at either. Contact seats for facilities heads and energy managers not published on either site.

operations: Seven campuses (Hatfield main, Hillcrest, Groenkloof, Prinshof, Onderstepoort, Mamelodi, GIBS Sandton) - 1 200 ha, 704 buildings, >1 000 000 m2 floor space, ~1 100 Facilities Management staff; ~55 000 students; supplied by City of Tshwane (Lynnwood substation for Hatfield/Hillcrest); 27 MVA of standby generation incl. six machines >1 MVA. Facilities Management (Technical Services) acquires electricity and runs energy monitoring; procurement via UP Department of Finance.
scale_note: ALREADY CONTRACTED: 25-year PPA with ATTSolar (Atterbury/Fledge Capital/MPower JV) signed Dec 2025 for a 10.5 MWp ground-mounted plant on UP land at Persequor Park (21.4 ha, >20 000 panels, ~22 225 MWh/yr, ~21 000 tCO2/yr) feeding the Lynnwood substation - sod-turning May 2026, commissioning Dec 2026, cuts UP carbon footprint >30% and priced below municipal tariff. Existing rooftop PV: 2 179 panels producing 1.36 GWh (2022, R1.75m saving) incl. 125 kWp Merensky Library and 161 kWp Technical Services under a 20-yr PPA with Next Renewable Generation (2017); 2 MW PV at Engineering 4.0 Hillcrest in municipal approval (2023). Total UP electricity not published (implied >70 GWh/yr from the 30% figure).

operations: Observing plateau 15 km from Sutherland at ~1 800 m on Old Fraserburg Road: 24 telescopes incl. SALT (11 m), Lesedi, MeerLICHT, ATLAS, PRIME, IRSF plus hostel/residences; HQ in Observatory, Cape Town. Supplied by Eskom on Ruralflex time-of-use tariff; 650 kVA site generator plus upgraded backups; UPS in domes. Winter heating of residences drives peak consumption.
scale_note: Small load: two 53 kWp grid-tied PV systems (2019 on SAAO site, 2020 on SALT stores roof, 40 kVA inverters) supplement Eskom; solar feasibility studied since 2011; wind considered for winter peaks; SALT goal to steadily increase renewable share by 2030. No MW/GWh figures published; no wheeling/PPA found. Remote location on Eskom rural network - wheeling would need Eskom-distribution wheeling.

operations: Four campuses - Auckland Park Kingsway (APK, main), Auckland Park Bunting Road (APB), Doornfontein (DFC) and Soweto; ~50 000 students; supplied by City Power (Soweto campus plagued by cable theft/outages). Operations division (COO) runs Central Technical Services, Property Management and campus infrastructure; Egoli natural gas used for residence heating with a 500 kW CHP trial planned at APB.
scale_note: Electricity ~48.9 GWh/yr across four campuses (2021). Solar PV on all four campuses: 4 450 panels / >1.7 MWp installed 2020-21 (RCSOL/Cronimet), ~4.3 GWh/yr (~9%); COO cites ~15% solar share by 2023; MEC approved a further 1 MWp PV plant at APK (Sept 2025); centralised backup power plant commissioned at Soweto replacing nine generators (2025); funding secured for a base-load gas-powered plant at APB; UJ Energy Plan 2023-2030 (draft Nov 2024) and ERWSus Plan 2022-2025; commitment to net-zero carbon by 2050; PV O&M tender Nov 2024; no wheeling/PPA found.

operations: Braamfontein East and West campuses, Parktown Education and Health Sciences campuses, Wits Rural Campus; ~40 000 students; city-based with limited roof/land space; supplied by City Power; standby diesel generators, co-generation and 14 solar installations run by OFMD Energy, Utilities and GMR Compliance unit; Campus Planning and Development runs capital projects and the PV/BESS tender.
scale_note: Peak demand ~14 MW in winter, ~4 MW minimum (Christmas Day); electricity spend not published (annual report). Solar: 14 installations, R30m invested, 1.7 MWp incl. solar hot water, just over 1 MWp PV (2024); no batteries; Solar PV Expansion and BESS term contract RFP 2026-2031 (Parktown Marang, Zylstra sport complex, Wits Club carport) issued 2026; sustainability strategy/vision 2050 approved 2023; approved budgets ~1/5 of what is needed for just-transition targets; 2024 statement that wheeling from private suppliers was not yet accessible - no wheeling/PPA found.

operations: Data centre on the CSIR Rosebank campus, Lower Hope Road, Rosebank, Cape Town (shared with NCPC-SA and CSIR Smart Places); Lengau 1 PFlop cluster (1 386 nodes, 24 racks) plus new ~4 PFlop direct-water-cooled 10-rack system (R400m, 2025), SEBOWA cloud and quantum access; chillers on stilts, new UPS & generator building (2021 RFP), two 1 MW on-site diesel generators (second commissioned March 2023) covering load-shedding; failover site for SA Weather Service; DSTI-funded; second DR data centre being sought. Supplied by City of Cape Town.
scale_note: Electrical load not published; scale implied by 2 x 1 MW generators and 24/7 100%-utilised cluster (order of 1-2 MW continuous, ~10-15 GWh/yr). NICIS business plan 2026-2030 states CHPC is one of the largest power consumers among SA research facilities and faces pressure to adopt renewable energy and efficient architectures. No solar or wheeling found; parent CSIR runs the Pretoria Energy Autonomous Campus programme.

operations: Main site at Faure (Old Faure Road, between Somerset West and Khayelitsha); ~300-340 staff; K=200 Separated Sector Cyclotron (operating ~6 000 h/yr) with two injector cyclotrons, 11 MeV F-18 cyclotron, 3 MV Tandetron, new 70 MeV IBA Cyclone 70P cyclotron (SAIF, inaugurated June 2023) with new transformers, MV/LV switchgear, rotary UPS and central chiller plant; also hosts the SKA Science Processing Centre site; radioisotope production to ~60 countries. Second site at Wits campus Johannesburg. Lat/lng from Wikipedia.
scale_note: Electricity consumption not published (cyclotron magnets, RF and cooling make it a multi-MW continuous load - SKAO puts its co-located SPC requirement at ~3.5 MW). SKAO reference design for the shared Faure SPC site: 2.2 MW PV + 6 MWh battery + RUPS + diesel, alternative shared UPS with iThemba, supplemented by wheeled energy (handed to SARAO/NRF, 2022). No iThemba solar PV, wheeling or PPA found; SAIF R&D capex ~US$13m phase 1.

commodity: State-owned nuclear research and radioisotope site
operations: Pelindaba complex on the R104 (Elias Motsoaledi St Ext), Madibeng Municipality, west of Pretoria: 640 ha inside the fence within a 2 362 ha estate; SAFARI-1 20 MW(th) research reactor (61 yrs old, ~287-300 operating days/yr, licence to 2030 with extension sought), NTP Radioisotopes hot cells and Mo-99 plant, Pelchem fluorochemical plants, ASME III nuclear manufacturing, fuel development lab, PBMR assets being transferred from Eskom; planned Multipurpose Reactor and SMR demonstration plant at Pelindaba; also runs Vaalputs waste site. Group NPAT R125.2m (2024/25).
scale_note: Site electricity consumption and spend not published in the IAR (Eskom-supplied; SAFARI-1 pumps, NTP and Pelchem plants make it a continuous multi-MW industrial load). No solar PV, wheeling or PPA found; Necsa's energy narrative is nuclear (2.5 GW procurement, SMR demo) rather than renewables, but its GE: Power and Industry has a distributed-renewables and CSIR Energy Autonomous Campus background. Government-grant plus commercial revenue funding; National Key Point security constraints for on-site generation.

operations: Karoo site on NRF-owned Meysdam/Losberg farms (135 000 ha Meerkat National Park) ~85 km from Carnarvon: 64-dish MeerKAT plus MeerKAT+ and SKA-Mid (133 dishes, 150 km spiral arms, first fringes end-2025, AA0.5 mid-2026); Klerefontein support base / SKA Engineering Operations Centre 10 km from Carnarvon (lat/lng given); Science Processing Centre in Cape Town co-located with iThemba LABS; SARAO HQ Pinelands, Cape Town. Power: Eskom 33 kV line (5 MVA at Carnarvon/Karoo substation) stepped to 22 kV site ring; three 1.25 MVA Euro-Diesel DRUPS (N+1, 2.5 MVA firm; R6.8m 3-yr maintenance awarded 2025), space for five units (6.25 MVA); 22 kV Carnarvon spiral with reactor/RMU tender 2026. Radio-quiet zone: all power plant must be RFI-shielded.
scale_note: MeerKAT ~4-5.4 MVA average, 6.7 MVA peak; SKA-Mid budget ~3.4 MW site (new 132 kV line option ~110 km from Kronos substation) plus ~3.5 MW Cape Town SPC; SKAO total ~13 MW continuous, >98% of its CO2. SKAO power strategy: hybrid PV/battery/diesel with grid, minimum 50% renewable fraction (pricing 80%) via IPP PPAs - SKAO approaching the market in 2026 for a renewable power station to run with the base diesel plant; prototype 131 kWp PV + 400 kWh Remote Power Station commissioning on-site early 2026 (target >80% RF) with standalone PV plants for the last 5-7 antennas on each spiral arm; 2.2 MW PV + 6 MWh battery reference design at the Cape Town SPC supplemented by wheeled energy. Small existing solar: Carnarvon visitor centre RFQ 2023. Grid power cost rising ~10% p.a.; SKAO capital excludes power infrastructure.
